sections.h2: Should a Kent owner list, sell alone or take cash?
sections.html:
A Kent seller has three routes: hire a listing agent, run the sale personally, or sell to a company that closes with its own money and no mortgage underwriting. The choice turns on the house itself, any tenants and your calendar.

  • Listing agent: works for a clean, updated house when weeks of showings and a loan approval are acceptable.
  • Owner run sale: saves the commission, though you price the house, schedule tours, hand over the state disclosure form and chase the deed paperwork.
  • Cash buyer: fits a worn house, a rental with a lease running, an inherited property or a hard closing date.

Just 40.8 percent of Kent households own the roof over their heads, the smallest share among Kent, Kettering, Lakewood and Lancaster. Much of what trades hands near campus is former student housing or small rentals, so buyers raise leases, inspections and licenses early.

sections.h2: How did Kent's housing market take shape?
sections.html:
Kent began as the mill village of Franklin Mills, settled in November 1805 by John and Sally Haymaker beside the Cuyahoga River. The Pennsylvania and Ohio Canal reached it in the 1830s and 1840s, and the Atlantic and Great Western Railroad put its repair shops there in 1864. The village took Marvin Kent's name that year and was incorporated on May 6, 1867.

Two things then reshaped the housing stock. The railroad shops closed in 1930, and Kent State, which began as a teacher training school in 1910, grew until the city went from 12,418 residents in 1950 to 28,183 in 1970. Haymaker Parkway, finished in 1975, eased traffic and blocked rail crossings downtown. Since 2008, public and private spending of about $110 million has gone into downtown projects such as Acorn Alley, a hotel and the Kent Central Gateway transit garage.

The result is a compact city of 9.22 square miles of land, about 3,060 people per square mile, with older frame houses near downtown and campus and postwar blocks farther out.

sections.html:
Federal estimates put Kent at 27,737 people in mid 2025, a 1.6 percent drop from the April 2020 base. The housing rows below are survey averages for 2020 through 2024.

sections.h2: How do the university, roads and weather affect a Kent sale?
sections.html:
Kent State University employs more people than anyone else here, and its 866 acre main campus on the southeast side shapes demand for houses within walking distance. Davey Tree Expert Company keeps its headquarters in the city and leads the private employers. Educational, health and social services account for 28.4 percent of the local workforce.

  • Schools: the Kent City School District covers most addresses, with four neighborhood elementary schools, Stanton Middle School and Theodore Roosevelt High School. The part of Kent south of State Route 261 belongs to the Field Local School District, so check which one serves a house before you advertise it.
  • Getting around: State Route 59 follows Main Street across downtown, State Route 43 carries traffic north and south, and Interstate 76 is about 3 miles south by way of exit 33. The PARTA bus system links Kent with Akron and Cleveland.
  • Distance: Akron is about 10 miles southwest and Cleveland about 30 miles northwest, so some buyers commute outward.

Kent sits in the secondary snowbelt, with about 36 inches of precipitation a year and thaws above 50 degrees in January and February. Check roofs, gutters and wet basements before listing, and receipts for any repairs are worth keeping with the disclosure form.

sections.h2: Which Kent offices should a seller contact before closing?
sections.html:
Start with the Building Division at 930 Overholt Road, phone 330-678-8107, which handles permits and the city's Exterior Maintenance Code. Ask whether any permit on your address was never closed out, because unfinished work can hold up a closing.

  • Rentals with four or more unrelated tenants: the Kent City Health Department, at 201 E. Erie Street, second floor, phone 330-678-8109, licenses these multiple use dwellings and investigates housing maintenance complaints under the city's Environmental Health and Housing Maintenance Code.
  • One and two family rentals: these are licensed through the Community Development Department, which can be reached at 330-678-8108. For code issues at unlicensed homes and small rentals, the city lists 330-678-8464.
  • Zoning: new construction, additions, accessory structures and signs need a zoning permit before work starts.

With tenants in place, tell the buyer which license applies and keep a copy for the closing file.

sections.h2: How does the deed transfer work in Portage County?
sections.html:
Portage County's Auditor runs the transfer step for Kent, a city that is the county's largest. The Auditor's Real Estate Department handles each deed ahead of recording. The Auditor's page prints the fee as $4.00 per $1,000.00 of the purchase price plus 50 cents per parcel, and it links the DTE 100 form.

Ohio Revised Code 319.202 has the buyer's side submit the statement of value, while the grantor pays the fee. The statement also asks whether the parcel gets a property tax reduction or farm use valuation, so know your answer before closing day. Parcel histories, valuations and sales data can be searched on the Auditor's site.

Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 asks owners of homes with one to four units to give each buyer a signed disclosure form. Transfers by an estate fiduciary, and a sale to someone who has already occupied the home for twelve months, appear among the exceptions. A buyer who never gets the form can back out, within a window that ends no later than closing.

sections.h2: Is a cash buyer a good fit for a worn or tenant occupied Kent house?
sections.html:
Cash is worth a look when certainty outranks the top price. Kent examples include a rental whose lease has months left, repairs that would stall a lender's appraisal, or a vacant house left behind by an estate.

Get any offer on paper, with the closing date, the party paying title and recording costs, and the buyer's rule if a walkthrough finds something new. Set two or three offers beside the net an agent would deliver after commission and repairs, and ask the Portage County Auditor what conveyance charge applies so the settlement sheet holds no surprises.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Kent house with student tenants still inside?
faqs.a: Yes. Read the lease for its end date, then either sell to a buyer who takes over the tenancy or plan the closing around move out. Confirm which Kent license covers the rental and hand the buyer copies of the lease and license.

faqs.q: Who collects the transfer fee when a house sells in Kent?
faqs.a: The Portage County Auditor collects it, and the city does not. The Auditor's page lists $4.00 per $1,000.00 of the purchase price plus 50 cents per parcel, and Ohio Revised Code 319.202 places the fee on the grantor.

faqs.q: Does selling my Kent home as is skip the disclosure form?
faqs.a: Usually no. Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 reaches one to four unit residential property, and a discounted as is price leaves the duty to complete the form in good faith untouched. Estate fiduciary sales and the other listed transfers are exempt.

faqs.q: Which school district does my Kent house belong to?
faqs.a: Most of Kent is in the Kent City School District, but addresses south of State Route 261 are in the Field Local School District. Ask the district or the county before you put a district name in a listing.

faqs.q: How can I find out what my Kent house is worth?
faqs.a: Search the parcel on the Portage County Auditor's property records for valuation and sales history, then compare an agent's opinion with written cash offers. The county figure serves tax purposes and often differs from a market price.
